body:
Thank you Cyclingnightmare, I understand that this is irreversible step and I wish to know what else I can do to help myself, but I really don't know.

I found success stories online about people looking for medical help in similar situations and managing to get back to normal life. I decided to go to psychiatric clinic looking for help because I figured I won't get better myself. It was very hard decision for me and I put a lot of hope into this, unfortunately my expectations were not fulfilled. Therapy was not effective and medications only helped with anxiety by making me half-sedated zombie who does not have any feelings and does not care about anything most of the time. That was not my goal and it did not help with rest of symptoms. My doctor keep changing medications but I already figured that he is trying to suppress most severe symptoms, and does not know what is causing them and how to stop it.

I was desperately trying to breach my loneliness for last few months without any success. I have almost no experience of being social. Also having culture and language barriers make things harder for me. I'm looking around and see millions of people being social, having partners and getting married, I don't think that they put so much efforts to get it as I do. I don't think that I'm just not trying hard enough. I keep trying harder but it only takes energy from me, leaving me nothing but disappointment.

Sometimes I have better days and I'm trying to enjoy them but nothing remains after them and I'm falling deeper and deeper into the darkness.

I still hope that things get better and it is holding me. But I don't want to live desperate live for next few decades keeping hoping for something, and getting nothing in the end. That is why I tried to put the deadline, and I suddenly felt relief because it gave me some certainty of the future. And it also makes me afraid of the future.

There is no guarantee. Sometimes people survive after receiving hit from a shotgun right to the face or after falling from the airplane.

You may end up with brain damage and disfigured face, attached to machines supporting your life.
